findings.evidence: Line 59 states the RHS with `tangentCoordChange I α β x`; lines 71-73 state it with `fderivWithin ℝ (extChartAt I β ∘ (extChartAt I α).symm) (Set.range I)`. Mathlib records the derivative form in the name, e.g. `hasFDerivWithinAt_tangentCoordChange` (mathlib/Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/VectorBundle/Tangent.lean:162).
findings.fix: Record the differing form in the name, e.g. `chartVolumeDensity_changeChart_fderivWithin`, keeping `chartVolumeDensity_changeChart` for the `tangentCoordChange` form.
findings.issue: `chartVolumeDensity_changeCoordinates` is synonymous with `chartVolumeDensity_changeChart` (line 55) — "change of chart" and "change of coordinates" name the same thing — yet the two lemmas differ precisely in the form of the Jacobian (`tangentCoordChange` vs `fderivWithin ... (Set.range I)`). Neither name says which form it gives.

findings.evidence: Statement at lines 82-85 applies the density at a point; `grep 'theorem \w*comp_symm'` in Mathlib gives only genuine compositions (`Topology/Homeomorph/Defs.lean:211 self_comp_symm (h : X ≃ₜ Y) : h ∘ h.symm = id`, `ModelTheory/Basic.lean:705 comp_symm ... (g.comp f).symm = f.symm.comp g.symm`). The naming conventions' symbol table lists `∘` ↦ `comp`.
findings.fix: Rename with `symm_apply` instead of `comp_symm`, e.g. `chartVolumeDensity_symm_apply_changeChart_fderivWithin` (matching whatever is chosen for line 67).
findings.issue: `chartVolumeDensity_comp_symm_changeCoordinates` uses `comp` for a statement containing no composition of the density: it is `chartVolumeDensity (I := I) α ((extChartAt I α).symm y)`, a pointwise application, not `chartVolumeDensity α ∘ (extChartAt I α).symm`. The naming dictionary maps `comp` to `∘`, and every Mathlib `comp_symm` lemma really has `∘`/`.comp`.

summary: The tangent-bundle matrix lemma and `chartVolumeDensity_changeChart` are named correctly and consistently with the existing `chartVolumeDensity_changeFrame`, but the two `changeCoordinates` names are defective: one is an English synonym of `changeChart` with no indication of what differs, and the other advertises a composition that does not occur in the statement.
